rows.title: FDM, PLA — 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.2 mm layer

hole_diameter_compensation.source: A vertical hole prints undersize: the extrusion's inside corner is laid on a polygon that cuts the circle, and the melt shrinks inward. +0.2 mm on the modelled diameter is the common community compensation for a 0.4 mm nozzle; the physical floor is 0, which is what a perfectly calibrated machine with hole compensation in the slicer needs. NOT measured here.

min_wall.source: One extrusion line at 0.42 mm (1.05 x nozzle) is the physical floor; two perimeters is the house minimum for anything structural.

min_boss_wall.source: A boss that a thread is formed into carries hoop stress, so it wants three perimeters rather than two. House rule, not measured.

layer_height.source: se-kind.md §Manufacturing modes, validated 2026-09-02 (perplexity-reasoning:292746): 0.2 mm is the confirmed default layer height for a 0.4 mm-nozzle-class machine — a process/nozzle figure, the same for every fdm material, not a per-material one. No distinct physical floor is recorded for this nozzle class (a thinner layer is a slicer choice, not a process failure), so 'physical' stays null rather than inventing one.

line_width.source: se-kind.md §Manufacturing modes, validated 2026-09-02 (perplexity-reasoning:292746): the confirmed working range for a 0.4 mm nozzle is 0.42-0.48 mm (~1.1x nozzle) — house is the midpoint of that range, 0.45 mm. Below ~0.3 mm the section flags the line as out-of-spec/weak, which is the physical floor. A 0.2 mm generic-slicer default is explicitly called out as wrong for this nozzle class. Process/nozzle figure, not per-material.

max_overhang.source: se-kind.md §Manufacturing modes, validated 2026-09-02 (perplexity-reasoning:292746): 45 degrees from vertical is the confirmed slicer-default overhang limit at 0.15-0.25 mm layers — the process/nozzle-class ceiling this row treats as the physical limit. House tightens to 40 degrees, the margin the section names as the pull toward the 0.32 mm layer ceiling. Process/nozzle figure, not per-material.

max_bridge.source: se-kind.md §Manufacturing modes, validated 2026-09-02 (perplexity-reasoning:292746): ~10 mm is the reliable community limit for PLA-class FDM bridging. Only one figure is published — no separate house-vs-physical margin recorded, so both tiers carry that one number rather than inventing a spread.

min_bed_contact.source: se-kind.md §Manufacturing modes describes min bed-contact only as 'a function of total print size', with no published figure or formula. Not characterized; never borrowed from a sibling material.

min_feature.source: se-kind.md §Manufacturing modes groups 'min wall/hole' together with no figure distinct from this row's own min_wall/min_boss_wall (the 2026-09-15 rung-3c seed, a different validation pass). Not characterized as its own facet; never borrowed.

min_hole.source: se-kind.md §Manufacturing modes groups 'min wall/hole' together with no published minimum-hole figure. Not characterized; never borrowed from a sibling row.

strength_z_ratio.source: se-kind.md §Manufacturing modes names the anisotropic strength vector only qualitatively ('weak across layers'), with no measured tensile-across-layers ÷ in-plane ratio. Not characterized; never borrowed.

max_build.source: Printer-specific (bed/gantry size), deliberately null in the generic rows — docs/backlog/se-print-implementer.md's own scope note. A house-tier refinement for a named printer is a later, data-only addition.

simp_pitch.source: Voxel pitch for realize(strategy='simp') (docs/backlog/structural-solution-space.md slice 4 bridge). A house figure is a trade-off between solve time (elements ~ volume / pitch^3; measured 2026-10-03: 1.4 s per iteration at 8,640 elements locally and 4.1 s on melchior, growing as about N^1.35, so about 20k elements is the practical ceiling at 100 iterations) and the smallest strut the field can carry (>= 2-3 pitches; compare min_wall) — not a process figure anyone has published, and this shop has not calibrated one yet. Null on purpose: the op demands pitch= (or a set_process_override on the block) until a calibrated house figure lands here; never a default in code.

min_member.source: The thinnest strut realize(strategy='simp') may leave (se-machine-design O2): it sets the sensitivity-filter radius to min_member/(2*pitch) elements, refuses a pitch above min_member/3, and defaults round= to min_member/3. The proposed house figure is 3 mm for a toy-scale part (about 3.5x min_wall, a strut that survives handling), but no SIMP part has been printed and handled yet. Null on purpose until the first test piece prints: without it the filter stays at 1.5 elements and the minimum member shrinks with the pitch; pass min_member= or set_process_override(field='min_member', value=<mm>).

min_clearance.source: The smallest in-place gap between two DOF-joined members that prints as two parts rather than fusing — realize(strategy='manufacture')'s in_place_clearance floor (docs/backlog/structural-solution-space.md slice 4 bridge, round B2). Community practice quotes 0.2-0.5 mm for a 0.4 mm nozzle depending on orientation (a vertical gap prints looser than a horizontal one), but this shop has not printed a gap ladder on this material and no per-orientation figure is published for it. Null on purpose: the op demands gap= while it is null and says the floor is uncalibrated; a set_process_override(field='min_clearance', value=<mm>) on the group root supplies one; never a default in code.
